transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-24 16:00 UTC | Duration 48m | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jamal Ortiz (CTO, Boreal), Ruth Park (Head Infra), Mateo Silva (ML Eng)

00:00:05 - Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — renewal terms, region residency ask, and the benchmark plan. Is that still correct?
00:00:18 - Jamal Ortiz: Yeah that's perfect. We have a board deadline for sign-off end of month so trying to lock numbers, and also Ruth wanted to confirm the private serving path for EU and APAC.
00:00:30 - Ruth Park: Yeah hi, thanks. Our two asks: one, Dedicated capacity minimums for predictable throughput; two, we need VPC + KMS integration for EU data. Also curious on degraded mode behavior.
00:00:45 - Priya Nair: Got it. We'll cover the Dedicated sizing and failover policy. Quick clarifier, when you say KMS are you referring to customer-managed keys via HSM or cloud KMS?
00:00:57 - Ruth Park: Prefer HSM-backed KMS, but cloud KMS is ok as long as key control is demonstrated. We have SOC two requirements and audit logging needs.
00:01:10 - Mateo Silva: And for the ML team, we need to validate latency at 95th percentile under our mix — mostly short prompts, lots of embeddings, occasional long generations.
00:01:21 - Alex Chen: Makes sense. For renewal, we're proposing a 12-month term with a Dedicated baseline that covers your steady-state QPS and a burst bucket for seasonal spikes. We'll send a worksheet with numbers.
00:01:33 - Jamal Ortiz: On that, can you explain how bursting works? Do we get pre-provisioned burst capacity or is it on-demand at a higher rate? Also how does routing to Hosted fallback look?
00:01:45 - Priya Nair: Sure. We have two mechanisms — scheduled burst reservations and on-demand bursting. Scheduled burst is reserved capacity you pay a lower commit for; on-demand bursts spin up from the pool and are billed at a premium. For critical paths we recommend scheduled burst. Fallback to Hosted API is automatic if Dedicated pool is fully saturated and policy allows, with model-variant fallback if sequence length or quantization differs.
00:02:10 - Ruth Park: Automatic fallback sounds risky for us — we need to control data plane for EU traffic.
00:02:16 - Alex Chen: That's fair — we can set a strict policy so EU traffic doesn't route to global Hosted endpoints; instead we have a geo failover to EU Dedicated standby or bring-up a cold standby in your VPC. We'll document policies.
00:02:30 - Jamal Ortiz: And the SLA? We need the latency SLO and credits model spelled out in the contract.
00:02:36 - Alex Chen: We'll include the SLA table. For Dedicated customers we target 99.9% uptime and token latency SLOs per route; credits scale with severity.
00:02:46 - Mateo Silva: Quick question — what's the KV cache behavior with Dedicated? We rely on prefix caching a lot.
00:02:52 - Priya Nair: The runtime supports prefix/K V cache — apologies often transcribed as KV cahce in our notes — persists in the serving tier and can be warmed during rollout. When you use VPC deployment, the cache is local to your Dedicated nodes; we have options for persistent checkpointing during node replacement.
00:03:12 - Ruth Park: Good, that addressed the caching. Next on KMS and audit logs: do you support customer-managed HSM with key rotation logs?
00:03:22 - Priya Nair: Yes, we support cloud KMS and HSM integrations; rotation is supported and audit logs flow to your SIEM via Syslog or Cloud Audit API. We'll drop the integration doc.
00:03:33 - Jamal Ortiz: Great. Mateo, shall we walk them through our traffic profile?
00:03:37 - Mateo Silva: Sure — mostly sub-200 token prompts, 40% embeddings, peak QPS around 1200 for short windows, steady-state ~300 QPS. Long generations are rare but critical for certain transactions. We'll send a sample trace and histogram.
00:03:54 - Alex Chen: Perfect — that helps sizing. For the benchmark, Priya, proposed 48-hour run emulating that mix?
00:04:02 - Priya Nair: Yes, 48-hour run including steady-state and synthetic burst windows. We'll capture 95/99th latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and token throughput. We'll use your sample corpus and the same quantization profile you intend to run.
00:04:14 - Jamal Ortiz: Will that be on Dedicated nodes in the EU region?
00:04:18 - Priya Nair: We can spin up a temporary Dedicated pool scoped to eu-west and ap-southeast for the test; there's a small test cost — we'll detail that in the worksheet.
00:04:28 - Ruth Park: Also need to confirm egress rules — our security team only allows outbound to certain endpoints. I'll provide allowed IP ranges.
00:04:35 - Alex Chen: Noted — Ruth to provide allowed-region list and egress constraints.
00:04:40 - Mateo Silva: One other thing — quantization and model variants. We have to ensure no regression in answer quality when you switch to int8 for cost reasons. How are regressions tested?
00:04:50 - Priya Nair: We have a quality monitoring pipeline tied to prompt suites. For any quantization or model change we run evals and regression alerts. We can lock a canary that runs both variants and compare BLEU/emd style metrics and manual review for business-critical prompts.
00:05:05 - Jamal Ortiz: Ok. On the legal side I need to know where data at rest lives and any subprocessor list.
00:05:12 - Alex Chen: We'll share the security and compliance pack — SOC2 report, subprocessor list, data residency map, and our standard DPA. Expect that in the email after the call.
00:05:21 - Ruth Park: Thanks. About contract pricing: we need to see a blended rate for tokens + dedicated node charge with burst credits. Also a path to reduce per-token cost after hitting volume thresholds.
00:05:33 - Alex Chen: The worksheet will show baseline committed node costs, token tiers, and step-down pricing after volume thresholds. For enterprise customers we can include quarterly true-ups.
00:05:44 - Jamal Ortiz: Can we also get an option for a 24-month term to reduce unit cost?
00:05:50 - Alex Chen: Yes, we can show both 12- and 24-month pricing options in the worksheet. We'll highlight breakpoints.
00:05:57 - Mateo Silva: For the benchmark, please capture 95th percentile latency for embeddings specifically; those are critical for our search stack.
00:06:05 - Priya Nair: Will do. We'll tag embeddings routes separately in the benchmark.
00:06:09 - Ruth Park: A note on failover: if EU Dedicated has an outage, we prefer warm standby in eu-west rather than routing to US hosted endpoints for compliance reasons.
00:06:19 - Priya Nair: We can configure a warm standby Dedicated pool in eu-west with automatic cutover. That reduces failover RTO and keeps data residency intact.
00:06:27 - Jamal Ortiz: How long to provision a warm standby?
00:06:31 - Priya Nair: Depends on instance type and hardware availability; typically warm standby is minutes to under an hour if pre-provisioned; cold standby could be longer. We'll capture provisioning times in the playbook.
00:06:41 - Alex Chen: Okay let me recap next steps: we'll send the renewal worksheet with 12/24 month options and SLA language (Alex). Redwood SE will run the 48-hour benchmark scoped to your traffic and regions (Priya). Ruth will send network constraints and allowed region list. Mateo will share traffic samples and 95th latency targets.
00:06:58 - Jamal Ortiz: Sounds good. Any blockers on our side?
00:07:02 - Ruth Park: No blockers, just internal approvals; we need the updated price by end of month to hit procurement cycle.
00:07:07 - Alex Chen: Understood. We'll prioritize.
00:07:10 - Mateo Silva: Quick aside — do you support per-route rate limiting that we can tune per tenant?
00:07:15 - Priya Nair: Yes, per-route quotas and token-level rate limits are supported. You can set per-API-key or per-tenant limits and the Console shows token breakdowns.
00:07:24 - Jamal Ortiz: Good. Any other questions?
00:07:27 - Ruth Park: One last thing — our security guy asked about encryption in transit on internal links between Dedicated nodes. Is that TLS mTLS?
00:07:36 - Priya Nair: We use mTLS for node-to-node and enforced TLS for client connections. We'll include technical details in the integration doc.
00:07:42 - Alex Chen: OK if no further questions we'll close and follow up with materials. Thanks everyone.
00:07:47 - Jamal Ortiz: Thanks, appreciate it.

Notes / imperfections: occasional words were mis-transcribed ("KV cahce", "S O C two"), speaker labels in the auto transcript sometimes appear as generic 'Speaker 1'. There was mild crosstalk when Ruth and Jamal answered simultaneously.

Call end: 16:48 UTC
